question: In Malory's Le Morte d'Arthur, Arthur fights his last battle against his own son Mordred. On the bare field, nearly every knight on both sides is killed. Arthur himself is mortally wounded there. What is the name of the battle where the fellowship of the Round Table falls?
context: Malory, Le Morte d'Arthur Book XXI ch.4. Camlann is the final battle where Arthur meets Mordred; the two kill each other. Roncesvalles is Roland's last stand in the Chanson de Roland. Badon is the earlier historical victory of the Britons over the Saxons. Bosworth is the real 1485 English battle where Richard III fell.  (Legend.)

question: The Chimera was one of a whole brood of famous monsters born to the same monstrous parents. Her siblings were the Nemean Lion that Heracles strangled, the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, and the three-headed hound Cerberus. Who were the parents of this whole brood?
context: Typhon, the storm-giant Zeus buried under Mount Etna, and Echidna, the half-woman half-serpent, produced the Nemean Lion, the Chimera, Cerberus, Orthrus, and the Lernaean Hydra between them. Uranus and Gaia are Sky and Earth; Cronus and Rhea are the Olympians' own parents; Nereus and Doris are the sea-parents of the fifty Nereids. Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimera_(mythology); Hesiod, Theogony 306-325.  (Legend.)

question: In Norse myth, Freyr is the god of sunshine, good weather, harvest, and peace. He was not born one of the Aesir — the warrior tribe of Odin and Thor who live in Asgard. Freyr belongs to the older tribe of fertility gods, and he was traded to the Aesir as a hostage after the two tribes made peace at the end of their great war. Which tribe is Freyr from?
context: Freyr, his father Njord, and his sister Freyja are the three Vanir hostages who came to live in Asgard after the Aesir-Vanir war. The Jotnar are the giants (their enemies); the Alfar are the elves; the Aesir are the tribe he was given to, not the one he came from. Snorri, Gylfaginning 23-24.  (Legend.)

question: At Ragnarok two of the great Aesir kings die at the jaws and fangs of two of Loki's own children -- one father-line producing the deaths of both. Odin is swallowed by Fenrir the wolf; Thor kills the second monster with his hammer Mjolnir but staggers only a few steps before dropping dead of its venom. How many steps does Thor take after killing Jormungandr before he falls?
context: Snorri, Gylfaginning 51; Voluspa 56: Thor kills the world-serpent Jormungandr with Mjolnir and staggers nine steps before dropping dead of its venom. Nine is a repeatedly sacred number in Norse cosmology (nine worlds of Yggdrasil, Odin's nine nights hanging on the tree). Odin, meanwhile, is swallowed whole by Fenrir; his son Vidar avenges him by tearing the wolf's jaws apart.  (Legend.)

question: In the Bible's book of First Kings, the prophet Elijah stands almost alone against the whole royal court of Israel. Eight hundred and fifty prophets of the Canaanite gods Baal and Asherah are fed at the private table of King Ahab's foreign wife — a Sidonian queen who has hunted the Lord's own prophets into hiding across the land. What is this queen's name?
context: 1 Kings 18:19 KJV -- 'the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel's table.' Jezebel is daughter of the Sidonian king Ethbaal and Ahab's queen. Bathsheba is David's wife; Delilah is Samson's betrayer; Athaliah is Jezebel's daughter who later seizes Judah's throne.

question: Beyond the veil of Solomon's Temple, in the windowless inner chamber, stood two enormous carved figures ten cubits tall. Their wings were stretched so wide that wingtip touched wall on either side and wingtip met wingtip in the middle of the room. Of what wood were those two figures carved?
context: KJV 1 Kings 6:23, 27: 'within the oracle he made two cherubims of olive tree, each ten cubits high ... the wing of the one touched the one wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall.' The tabernacle furniture was acacia; the roofs and paneling were cedar; the flooring was cypress.

question: The Tuatha De Danann arrived in Ireland concealed in dark clouds, and the two peoples met in a great battle on a plain in what is now County Mayo. In this battle the Fir Bolg champion Sreng, in a single sword-stroke, cut off the right hand of the Tuatha king Nuada. What is that battle called?
context: The First Battle of Moytura (Cath Maige Tuired Cunga) was fought at Cong in County Mayo, where Sreng struck off Nuada's hand. Clontarf (1014) is history, not myth. The Second Battle of Moytura is later, against the Fomorians. Ventry is a battle of the Fianna cycle.  (Legend.)

question: The old Irish new year fell on the night of November 1. Farmers brought the cattle down from summer fields. On that night, the wall between our world and the Otherworld was said to grow thin. Later this night became what English speakers call Halloween. What is the Irish name for it?
context: SAMHAIN (November 1) is the ancestor of modern Halloween -- one of the four quarter-festivals of the Irish year. Bealtaine (May 1) opens summer; Lughnasadh (August 1) is the harvest festival of Lugh; Imbolc (February 1) is the spring festival of Brigid. Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samhain.  (Legend.)
